S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent binge-eating episodes with a sense of loss of control, followed by recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors intended to prevent weight gain. It is typically accompanied by strong overvaluation of weight or shape, may fluctuate in severity over time, and is distinguished from binge-eating disorder by compensatory behaviors and from anorexia nervosa by the broader weight range in which it usually presents, though careful differential assessment is needed when weight is significantly low.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in living condition (new home, remodeling, deterioration of neighborhood or home)
patient.stressor: Seventeen months ago, Adam moved into a small apartment near the tourist district while his longtime Jamestown rental was being remodeled, leaving him without his usual kitchen setup and pushing more of his meals into late-night takeout after shifts. At first he framed the change as temporary and tried to offset the irregular eating with extra trail runs, but over the year he began having repeated episodes of eating far more than he intended after work, followed by both exercise-based compensation and purging to keep his weight down. Even as coworkers commented that he looked too thin, his fear of gaining weight became tied to feeling presentable for guests, jam sessions, and a possible shift-lead role. He sought psychiatric care after recognizing the pattern during a mindfulness journaling exercise and asking his primary care clinician for a referral before the behavior became more visible at work.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: Even when people at the venue tell me I look too lean, I get panicky if my pants feel a little tighter or the scale is up a pound, like guests and coworkers will notice right away and think I let myself go.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: After a bad night of eating, I’ll make myself run extra miles on the trail the next morning or skip breakfast before my shift, even when I’m tired, because it feels like I have to undo it.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: Sometimes after I get home and eat too much takeout or snacks, I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up so it won’t sit in me and turn into weight.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: I came in because after late shifts I’ll stop for food and then keep going at home—like a full takeout meal, chips, sweets, whatever’s in the apartment—and afterward I’m shocked by how much I ate.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start on those nights, it’s like I’m watching myself from the outside, telling myself to put the food away, but my hands just keep opening containers until everything is gone.

add_requirements.The binge eating and inappropriate compe: Since the apartment move settled into a routine, most weeks I have at least one late-night episode where I eat way past what I meant to, and then I try to make up for it by throwing up, skipping breakfast, or forcing a long run.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still showing up for work, but I’ve started dodging after-shift meals with coworkers and planning my mornings around undoing the night before instead of resting or handling errands.
